thread:
release-bot: Starting staged rollout: service=serving-api, image=redwood/serving:1.12.3, target=5% global, prebake=10m, change_window_end=2024-08-07T20:30:00Z. Monitoring hooks attached.

morgan: Confirming change window and that eu-west is included in the 5% sample?

release-bot: yes — sampling is global. eu-west included. Canary group defined by user_id hash.

alejandra: seeing a small tail-latency bump in eu-west at ~19:34 UTC on the first 1% samples, tail from 220ms -> 480ms. Not present in us-west.

samir: can you post the query histogram?

alejandra: ```
19:33:50 metric=tail_latency p99=480ms p95=160ms reqs=120
19:33:55 metric=tail_latency p99=470ms p95=155ms reqs=135
```

ops-bot: metrics dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/serving-api/rollouts/1909871234 (auto snapshot).

lee: we should consider pausing the ramp and pinning eu-west to v1.12.2 while we investigate. If it's a tokenizer/kv-cache thrash that will only impact eu.

morgan: agree. Hold global ramp at 5%. If ops want to pin region, prefer region-level split instead of full rollback.

samir: +1. Two-action plan: (1) pause further percent increases, (2) pin eu-west to previous variant. Anyone object?

alejandra: no objection. I want to run a small replay of failing traces against the canary binary first.

deploy-bot: Running command: `deploy-bot set-traffic --service serving-api --target-image redwood/serving:1.12.3 --percent 5 --action pause`

deploy-bot: OK — rollout paused at 5%. No further automatic increases will occur. (cmd id: cb2f9)

deploy-bot: Running command: `deploy-bot pin-region --service serving-api --region eu-west --image redwood/serving:1.12.2 --reason "tail latency spike on canary"`

deploy-bot: OK — eu-west pinned to redwood/serving:1.12.2. Traffic split: eu-west->v1.12.2 (pinned), rest-of-world 5%->v1.12.3. (cmd id: cb2fa)

morgan: Good. Alejandra, can you run the trace repro? If repros, escalate to runtime team. If not, we can continue heat probe after 30m.

alejandra: started a small replay now, will post summary in ~8m.

samir: I'll open rollback runbook and prepare quick rollback steps in case pin doesn't stop errors. Link to runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/runbooks/serving-api-rollback.

lee: note for on-call: if error-rate in eu-west > 1% or p99>400ms for 10m, we escalate to full rollback.

alejandra: replay shows similar tail in a small subset — looks like kv-cache misses on long contexts. Opening a short issue for runtime: https://issues.redwood.com/ISSUE-4821

morgan: ok, action items: alejandro (runtime) + infra on the issue, hold global ramp, eu pinned. Re-evaluate at 20:05 UTC.

samir: putting a soft-stop vote: stop further rollout until next check-in. react with :thumbsup: to stop, :white_check_mark: to continue.

lee: :thumbsup:

morgan: :thumbsup:

alejandra: :thumbsup: (until runtime triage completes)

deploy-bot: Vote tally: stop=3, continue=0. Outcome: STOP.

release-bot: Noted — rollout remains paused at 5% with eu-west pinned. Will update release notes with rollback-safe-steps.

morgan: I'll notify PM and customer success for the affected tenants in eu-west. Posting a short blurb to #customer-notify after we have the triage summary.

alejandra: triage update: root cause likely kv-cache eviction under longer prompt contexts; runtime has a patch candidate to be validated in a dev cluster. ETA for candidate test: ~45m.

samir: if candidate validates, we can unpin and resume ramp with a targeted 2% increment and extra telemetry. If not, schedule a full rollback to v1.12.2 for all regions.

morgan: good plan. Next check-in at 20:05 UTC. For now, thread closed for roll decision until triage finishes. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
